Side effects

AOD-9604 side effects

In the developer's oral and IV trials, side effects of AOD-9604 were similar to placebo; headache was the most common, and gut symptoms and colds were also frequent.1 FDA identified no human data for injection under the skin, found too little information to support long-term safety, and has open concerns about immune reactions and the tumors reported in one trial.2

Where the data come from

All human safety data for AOD-9604 come from six randomized, placebo-controlled trials that its developer, Metabolic Pharmaceuticals, funded between 2001 and 2006, in 893 adults given the peptide by mouth or by vein.1 The safety summary was written by employees or consultants of the developer.2 The lists below follow that record, then the gaps and warnings FDA described in its 2024 review.

Common side effects (seen with AOD-9604 and placebo alike)

  • Headache: the most common adverse event across the trials.1 Counting all groups, including placebo, it affected 42.6% of participants during the 12-week trial and 25.9% during the 24-week trial.1
  • Gut symptoms: diarrhea, flatulence, nausea and increased appetite were common in the oral trials.1 Diarrhea affected 9.0% of all participants in the 12-week trial and 7.8% in the 24-week trial.1
  • Colds and back pain: in the 24-week trial, nasopharyngitis affected 17.1% of participants and back pain 8.2%, across all groups.1
  • First IV study: 12 of 15 healthy men reported 29 events across all treatments, including headache, fatigue, low blood sugar, dizziness, nasopharyngitis and cough, plus single reports of injection-site bruising, injection-site pain and an application-site reaction.1 The events were spread evenly between AOD-9604 and placebo.1
  • Overall rate: in the 24-week trial, 83.2% of the placebo group and 75.6% of the 0.25 mg group had at least one adverse event.1

Less common, judged possibly related

  • Euphoria: 5 of 23 obese men reported mild or moderate euphoria during IV AOD-9604 periods, and none during placebo.1
  • Chest tightness: one severe feeling of chest tightness after a 50 microgram per kg IV dose.1
  • Serious diarrhea: one case at the 54 mg oral dose in the single-dose study, even though the paper's abstract states that no related serious adverse event occurred.1

Serious adverse events

  • Tumors in the 12-week trial: five serious events, all in AOD-9604 groups: basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma and a lipoma in the 20 mg group, breast cancer in the 5 mg group and melanoma in the 10 mg group.1 The investigator judged none related; FDA says there is not enough information to show they were unrelated.12
  • 24-week trial: 18 of 502 people (3.6%) had at least one serious adverse event, spread similarly across groups: 8 on placebo, 3 on 0.25 mg, 1 on 0.5 mg and 6 on 1 mg.1
  • FDA reporting system: FDA's adverse event database returned no AOD-9604 reports in a search through January 7, 2024, and FDA notes that a lack of reports does not mean a substance is safe.2

Gaps in the evidence

  • Injection under the skin: FDA found no human data for subcutaneous use, although most clinics offering AOD-9604 sell injections or oral products.2
  • Long-term use: the longest human exposure was 24 weeks of oral tablets.1 FDA says there is not enough information to support long-term safety, and it identified no human study of how the body absorbs or clears the peptide.2
  • Pregnancy: FDA identified no developmental or reproductive toxicity studies,2 and the 12-week trial enrolled only women who could not become pregnant.1
  • Cancer risk in animals: FDA identified no carcinogenicity studies.2

Warnings

  • Immune reactions: FDA is concerned about immunogenicity, because AOD-9604 can form aggregates and carry peptide-related impurities.2 FDA's safety-risks page says compounded AOD-9604 may pose a significant immunogenicity risk for certain routes of administration.3
  • Serious events of unclear cause: the same page says FDA has identified serious adverse events that may be associated with AOD-9604, though causality is not clear.3
  • Product quality: FDA found that the certificates of analysis submitted to it, and public sources, lacked specific tests for impurities, aggregates and microbes, and that endotoxin testing for injectable use was lacking; it considers AOD-9604 not well characterized.2
  • Animal toxicology: developer-linked authors reported no genotoxic or toxicological concerns after oral dosing for 6 months in rats and 9 months in monkeys.4 FDA's review of those studies found signals suggesting harm to bone health in rats, possible liver toxicity signals in monkeys and equivocal mutagenic signals in genotoxicity tests.2
  • Athletes: WADA prohibits AOD-9604 at all times,5 and anti-doping scientists have validated a urine test that detects it down to 50 pg/mL.6

Frequently asked questions

Is AOD-9604 safe?

Safety is only partly known. In developer-funded oral and IV trials lasting up to 24 weeks, side effects were similar to placebo, mostly headache, gut symptoms and colds.1 But FDA concluded in 2024 that safety information is limited: it identified no human data for injection under the skin, found too little information to support long-term safety, warned that injected routes may carry a particular risk of immune reactions, and noted unresolved bone, liver and genotoxicity signals in animal studies.2

Can AOD-9604 cause diarrhea?

Yes. Diarrhea was among the common complaints in the oral trials. Counting every group, placebo included, it affected 9.0% of participants in the 12-week trial and 7.8% in the 24-week trial.1 People given the highest oral dose, 54 mg a day for 7 days, had more diarrhea, flatulence and headaches, and in a single-dose study one serious case of diarrhea at 54 mg was judged possibly related.1

Will AOD-9604 mess up bloodwork?

In the developer's trials, AOD-9604 did not change IGF-1 or glucose tolerance compared with placebo, and no antibodies against it were found.1 Blood counts, blood chemistry, urinalysis, lipids and ECGs were checked before and after treatment, with a safety profile the authors called indistinguishable from placebo.1 Testosterone was not among the reported measures,1 and FDA identified no human data for injection under the skin.2

Did AOD-9604 cause cancer in trials?

That is not known. In the 12-week trial, five people in AOD-9604 groups had tumors reported as serious adverse events: basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, a lipoma, breast cancer and melanoma.1 The investigator judged them unrelated, partly because none occurred at the highest dose, but FDA says the information is insufficient to decide.12 FDA also found no animal studies of cancer risk.2
